newsitem.title: UK: Woolwich steps up insurance activities.
newsitem.headline: Woolwich steps up insurance activities.

text.p: Britain's Woolwich Building Society said on Wednesday it planned to make its name synonymous with general insurance, with a significant increase in insurance activities in 1997 as part of its diversification strategy.

Using its joint venture insurance operation set up with Legal & General in September 1995, it plans to expand distribution, develop traditional products such as buildings and contents insurance and introduce new business areas, particularly motor and travel insurance.

Existing insurance services contributed over 11 million stg profit in the first nine months of last year and group operations director Lynne Peacock said there was strong organic growth potential in the insurance area.

"While the Woolwich has typically arranged household insurance for around 75 percent of its eligible borrowers, less than one percent of Woolwich's 3.5 million investing customers currently buy insurance from the Society," she said.
"We've done our homework and now we are ready for the step change in our general insurance activities."

Woolwich plans to have a specialist general insurance adviser in every high street branch by year end. Its new travel insurance, Holidaywise, will be available in UK branches from January 20 while Woolwich motor insurance will be on offer from the end of the month.
The company is also planning to develop a direct telephone operation.
The mutually owned building society, the third largest in the country with assets of more than 30 billion stg, plans a three billion stg stock market flotation in July.
